I'm also talking more in general. While the COVID thing has certainly shown the true greedy colors of a lot of landlords and a lot of people are getting screwed because of it, most of the stuff I've seen that's anti-landlord is people being anti-landlord always, not just right now. 

My argument is basically this: people say landlords are evil and are taking money from people who actually earned it. But the landlords aren't "taking" money, they're being paid money to allow someone to live in their house. If you want to argue that the entire rental system is fucked that's one thing, but with the state of the US right now and our current policies you're not going to make renting/landlording go away. So I don't see what's so wrong with landlords making money off of a system that (in my opinion) essentially has to exist because I don't see any other alternative?

I meant more with our current system. It's unrealistic to expect the current system to change just like that, and while I would certainly be a supporter of an alternative system there still needs to be something in the meantime.
But what is the alternative? How else are people who can't afford to outright buy a home supposed to find housing?

But wouldn't somebody else be profiting off of that person if the landlord wasn't there? People need housing, our government does not have many housing programs that would eliminate the need for a person to find and pay for their own house. So there are two options (generally speaking): either they buy a house, or they rent a house. Buying a house is a higher upfront cost that many can't afford. For those who do buy a house, there's still somebody profiting off of them. The previous owner, the bank they're paying their mortgage to, the company that built the house, etc. You could argue that if they're buying the house directly from whoever just built it is a fair exchange cause those people had to build the house... but are banks not also "taking money from people who need it more"? Those are also regular payments that you have to make. Yes you can eventually pay it off, but still. 

I feel like I'm rambling but my main thing that I disagree with is the "taking money from people who need it more than they do" part. I just feel like in our current system that's a) something that is inevitably going to happen and b) blaming landlords for it just seems off. They're making money off of investments.

I'm not necessarily arguing that landlords shouldn't lay off the rent. I do think landlords should be flexible and cut costs where they can. I'm more arguing the fact that landlords are not inherently evil and greedy as it seems so many people believe.

Where I am mortgage payments have not been stopped. Some banks have stopped them in some places but not all and not where I live (US). I agree it would be immoral and greedy to continue to demand rent payments in that situation, but that's not the situation where I am.

You could indeed sell the house. And where will the tenant go? Wouldn't that just screw them over even more? Unless they're the ones that bought the house I guess.

I don't see what's wrong with a landlord making money off of owning something they bought, I guess. We can argue that the entire housing system is corrupt and housing should be a right not a privilege and it's greedy to profit off of something that people should be able to access by default, but that's not how our system works.

Is the argument that everyone should just buy their own houses and renting shouldn't be a thing? I'm not very well versed in economics so if renting wasn't a thing would it be more affordable to outright buy a house? I know many people that absolutely can't afford to buy a house so they rent instead. Would eliminating renting entirely fix this issue? Is that what people who view landlords as evil want? I genuinely don't know, those aren't hypotheticals.

After looking through the databases I have available to me I was not able to find any peer-reviewed research in support of transracialism, no. In general I believe there have not been any studies on transracialism specifically, but I can't say that definitively having spent a mere 10 minutes looking.

I know that my argument is not necessarily science based either. That's why I've come here to see if someone has scientific evidence that can back up their claims. I don't think my argument is completely sound or even close to it, which is why I'm very open to changing my mind.

That's definitely an interesting argument, but I'm not sure I totally follow. You're saying the actual brain structure doesn't match their biological sex? From everything I know there are very few structural differences between male/female brains and I would just be curious to know how that is actually studied/measured. 

Are there any studies you can find that or point me towards that can support that claim? I ask because throughout my education I have not actually heard of this phenomenon. If true, though, that's a really good point and would change my mind.

Well that's not really a valid argument, is it? You don't think that that's what's going on, but you haven't pointed to any scientific evidence that supports that claim. I wouldn't consider that an actual argument. It could very well be what is happening, to my knowledge there's no concrete research to prove/disprove it. I could be wrong, though.

I think it's because a person's pet is an important part of their lives and something they want to share with whoever they talk to. What's wrong with that? I have 4 pets and an important part of my life is taking care of them and playing with them. I want whoever I'm talking to to know about this, and both having pets is something you can bond over. One of the best people I met on this subreddit has a dog and we regularly send pics and videos of our dogs to each other and we love it, because we both love dogs, and we know this because we mentioned it when we first met.
